resources.string: ZenithW aims to make saving online media, organizing files and handling everyday media tasks accessible in one place. The Android app brings that approach directly to your phone and tablet. Start by sharing or pasting a link, then prepare the video, audio or subtitles you need. The web and Windows editions are also part of the same project.

ZenithW offers an ad-free, open-source experience. You can use the Android app without creating a ZenithW account. The goal is to keep download and file options understandable while making advanced preferences accessible. You can help development by reporting bugs, contributing translations or code, and supporting the project voluntarily if you wish.

The download panel shows the title, artwork, duration and available formats provided by the source. Start with automatic selection or change the quality, video codec and file format. MP4, MKV and WebM are available for video. The resolutions and audio quality you can choose depend on the streams the source actually offers. Open the format list when you need to inspect individual source formats.

Audio mode offers M4A, MP3, Opus, WAV and FLAC output. If the source provides manual or automatic subtitles, you can select their languages and format. Artwork, metadata and chapter options help you customize the file. The advanced section includes trimming, naming, network, speed and custom yt-dlp options. Format compatibility and the information supplied by the source determine which items can be embedded.

Collect several links in the queue, select items from a playlist, and adjust task order or priority. Set concurrent downloads, scheduling and network requirements to suit your usage. You can pause and resume waiting tasks and follow processing stages and progress. When a task fails, its details and process log help you understand what needs another attempt.

The library and history provide search, sorting and filters to find saved media. Open or share files, mark favorites and organize them into collections. History retention and the output folder are controlled in settings. Removing a history entry and deleting a file from the device are separate actions. Moving or deleting a file in another app can affect whether its history entry can open it.
Work with media on your device

Local media tools can convert files you select on your device, extract audio, mute a video and trim a range. Suitable files also support container changes and creating GIFs or animated WebP images. Subtitle tools include SRT and VTT conversion, time offsets, and adding or burning subtitles into supported video outputs.

You choose the input file and where to save the result. FFmpeg performs conversion on your device. Processing time and output size depend on duration, resolution, codec and your chosen settings. Re-encoding can use substantial processing power and battery, and temporary files may need free storage. Available operations depend on the codecs and filters included with the app’s engine.

Some sources require you to sign in to their own service to download content you can access. Save a session through the in-app browser or import a Netscape-format cookie file. These profiles are encrypted with Android Keystore and stored on your device. Your selected session is used for the relevant task’s connections to the source. The source website’s access requirements still apply.

Change the selected session or delete saved profiles whenever needed. If the selected profile is deleted, new or retried tasks require you to reconnect. You can choose anonymous downloading explicitly. Cookies can provide account access, so treat them as private information and take care when sharing cookie files. Review diagnostic logs for personal information before sharing them as well.

Downloads depend on source support and the content currently available. Removed or private content, login requirements, regional restrictions, request limits and website changes can affect a task. DRM-protected streams are outside the supported downloads. Engine updates can adapt to some source changes. Availability of every link, or the same quality for every video, cannot be guaranteed.

Check content permissions and the source’s terms before saving or sharing media. Use these tools for your own content and media you have permission to download. If a task fails, review the selected session, format, connection and task details. Reporting an issue in the source repository with your device, app version and a log stripped of sensitive information helps others reproduce the problem.
